results.note: Zen Beach at sunset (March 2025): people wading in the shallows and a paddleboarder under a sunset sky. Geotagged about 50 m from Grasshopper Beach Bar, which sits on Zen Beach per OpenStreetMap. Replaced the given candidate, which showed the main Sri Thanu beach (2008 photo), not Zen Beach. The 4:3 frame crops to 16:9 keeping the people and the sky.

The given candidate, kept: the Secret Party at night, a crowd in front of the red star-shaped stage under jungle trees. The organiser's small SECRET PARTY logo sits in the bottom-right corner and stays in the card crop (about 60 px wide on a phone). Every other image I found was a text flyer (26 phangan.events event posts, 4 megatix listings). secretpartykohtao.com and secretpartythailand.com are 'Coming Soon' pages.

results.license: venue photo via entrix.vip (the event's ticket page)
results.note: Night fire show at Hii Festival: a burning 'Hii KOH TAO' sign, a steel-wool fire spinner and sparks. Portrait, with the festival logo printed near the bottom (below y=1570). I ran the project's default 640x360 attention crop on it: it shows only the sign and sparks, no logo. If a crop is ever set by hand, keep it above the logo (BAND 560 works). Replaced the candidate, a soft portrait video frame of the hilltop Hii sign with a phangan.events caption. The official site hiifestivalkohtao.com has a good crowd photo, but its big logo sits in the middle of the crowd. The site's gallery is down because its Cloudinary account is disabled.

Drone shot at sunset of Sai Thong Beach, the festival's venue: palms, sand, rocks and sea. From the festival's own 'Sai Thong Beach - Koh Tao' gallery, with no watermark. Replaced the candidate, a text-heavy collage flyer. The festival's party photos all carry an 'lbmf' watermark (about 60 checked across 5 albums), so I chose this clean venue photo. It is square; the default crop keeps the palms and the beach. Warning: the festival homepage loads upload/1764142773.phtml and upload/album-1788851489.php as CSS backgrounds. These look like scripts planted on a hacked site; I did not open them. Be careful about linking leobeachmusicfestival.com in the guide.
